It is your requirements, with the exact values to use verbatim.

## Context
- Work from: C:\Users\mariu\ruflo-wt-console-win (git worktree, branch fix/console-windows). Plugin dir: plugins/ruflo-console. Windows 11, Node 24.
- Earlier tasks: A2 created `hooks/data/paths.ts` (isAbsolutePath, joinPath, samePath, isWindowsPath, trimTrailing, hasParentSegment, normalizePath, below); A3 added homeOf. Use these; do not duplicate them.
- Why: every console disk write today goes through `host.run` with `uname -s`, `dd`, `install -D`, `sh -c`, `mkdir -p`, `cp --no-clobber` (hooks/data/write-flavor.ts, append-argv.ts, wf-file.ts:84-104, activity-io.ts:122,132). In Claude Code's process environment on Windows none of uname/dd/sh/install/mkdir.exe/cp.exe is on PATH (only Git\cmd), and `flavorOfPlatform('win32')` returns 'gnu' (write-flavor.ts:27-28) so a GNU dd argv is built and fails. Result: Events persistence, Timeline lanes, autopilot journal, ADR files, exports and .gitignore writes all fail on Windows.
- Host file API available to hooks (engine declaration, exact): `$.fs.read(path, opts?)` (text by default; rejects over 4 MiB), `$.fs.write(path: string, text: string): Promise<void>` (whole new content; rejects over 4 MiB), `$.fs.list(path?): Promise<FsEntry[]>` (entries with names/mtimeMs and kind info), `$.fs.exists(path): Promise<boolean>`. A path is relative to the working directory or absolute. Look at how hooks/host.ts declares the Host interface and how register.ts `hostOf` binds `$` members, and follow that pattern. If you need to know FsEntry's exact fields, grep this file: C:/Users/mariu/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/bundled-skills/2.1.286/e9359f1bd6280f63d9d038bce106683a/plugin-authoring/types/claude-code.d.ts for `FsEntry` and `fs: {` (do not read the whole 18k-line file).
- Whether `$.fs.write` creates missing parent folders is not documented: test it is not possible in vitest; design 'create-dirs' so it is correct either way (e.g. nothing to do if write creates parents; otherwise report a clear "cannot create folder" refusal) and say which you assumed in the report.
- Controller ruling (binding): host-fs append rotates exactly where the existing GNU path rotates (same files, same threshold); anywhere the GNU path does not rotate, an append whose result would pass 4 MiB is refused with a clear error.
- The Linux GNU and darwin/BSD argv must be byte-identical to today — snapshot today's argv in a test BEFORE changing code.
- Existing related specs: tests/write-argv.spec.ts, tests/events-persist.spec.ts, ADR write specs (adr-write.spec.ts). Some write-argv/adr-write cases fail on this machine only because of symlink EPERM or Windows file modes or a '>' in a file name — compare against the base and do not count those as regressions.
- vitest: from plugins/ruflo-console run `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/<file>.spec.ts` (node_modules is a git-ignored junction — never commit it).
- Skip the brief's manual Windows check step (Step 5) — the controller will do it; note that in your report.
- No new dependencies. Touch only plugins/ruflo-console. Do not push.
- Commit message: `fix(console): disk writes work on Windows through the host file API`, ending with exactly `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <[REDACTED:email]>`.

handback.t:
Status: DONE for fix round 1 (both Important issues). Not pushed.
Commit: fcfef3678 "fix(console): autopilot kill flag can be cleared on Windows; document host-fs create window".

Issue 1, KILL flag, implemented as ruled:
- `KILL_CLEARED = 'cleared'` is exported from `hooks/data/ap-envelope.ts`.
- On host-fs, `clearKill` rewrites the KILL file with that marker. On POSIX/GNU it still runs the same `rm -f` argv.
- `killSeen` is the only place that reads the file, and only on host-fs. A missing file is not set, exactly the marker is not set, and anything else (empty included) is set. All listed callers go through `killSeen`, so none needed changes.
- One addition beyond the ruling: on host-fs `stopNow` now rewrites the flag empty instead of `touch`. A `touch` leaves an existing file's content alone, so a second stop after a clear would have kept the marker and been missed. The cycle test caught this.

Issue 2: the `write-via.ts` header and `wf-file.ts` now say host-fs create-excl, create-dirs and copy-no-clobber are check-then-write. They also say the host API has no O_EXCL and that a file appearing in the window is overwritten.

Tests: 3 new in `tests/write-flavor.spec.ts`:
- the full cycle on host-fs (stop, seen, start, not seen, stop again, seen), using the real `startSpec` run;
- a marker table;
- a gnu test pinning that `clearKill` still runs `rm -f -- <KILL>`.
RED: with the round-1 code reverted, 2 of 23 failed. GREEN: all 23 pass.

Covering specs (write-flavor, ap-live, ap-adapt, ap-complete, ap-core, ap-parallel, ap-review, write-argv): 142 passed, 1 skipped, 8 failed. The 8 are the same pre-existing write-argv real-disk POSIX failures as on base.

Minor review items were not touched.
